title: Human Map Upgrade — Fisher Geometry, Profile Likelihood and Experiment Design
status: archive-generated methodological extension of the Human Map; statistical identifiability framework, not a validated consciousness biomarker
abstract: The Human Map already requires latent-state identifiability and measurement invariance. This upgrade separates structural identifiability from practical identifiability and turns weak parameter directions into an experiment-design problem. The Fisher information matrix diagnoses local sensitivity and sloppy directions near a fitted point, but is not treated as universal proof of identifiability; nonlinear likelihoods, latent-state label symmetries and finite data can make local quadratic approximations misleading. Profile likelihood and synthetic parameter recovery therefore become practical checks. The model advances only when the parameters, latent combinations or predictions needed for its scientific claims are actually constrained by the measurements used.

likelihood_geometry.fisher: I_ab(theta)=E_theta[s_a s_b], equivalently -E_theta[partial_a partial_b log p(y|theta)] under standard regularity assumptions
likelihood_geometry.meaning: Large information means the modeled data distribution changes strongly under a small parameter perturbation; a local null direction indicates degeneracy under that experiment.

identifiability.structural: Ask whether distinct parameter values can produce exactly the same ideal noise-free observable distribution/trajectory.
identifiability.practical: Ask whether finite noisy data constrain the parameter or relevant combination to a scientifically useful range.
identifiability.latent_warning: Label switching, scale/rotation freedom and redundant latent dimensions must be constrained before interpreting Fisher geometry.

fisher_diagnostics.rank: Rank deficiency indicates locally unidentifiable directions under the chosen experiment, subject to regularity/parameterization assumptions.
fisher_diagnostics.eigenvectors: Small-eigenvalue directions identify weak parameter combinations.
fisher_diagnostics.condition_number: Large eigenvalue spread indicates sloppiness but depends on parameter scaling.
fisher_diagnostics.cramer_rao_boundary: The inverse Fisher information is a local precision comparator under theorem assumptions, not proof of global identifiability.

profile_likelihood.definition: Fix theta_j=v, reoptimize nuisance parameters and record the resulting likelihood profile PL_j(v).
profile_likelihood.meaning: Closed finite regions support practical identification; broad plateaus/open regions reveal compensation and weak identification that a local Hessian can miss.

prediction_identifiability.principle: Poorly identified parameters can still yield a tightly constrained prediction if many parameter combinations imply nearly the same observable.
prediction_identifiability.rule: Separate prediction certainty from parameter interpretation; do not assign biological/spiritual meaning to unconstrained latent parameters.

experiment_design.goal: Choose measurements/interventions that add information in the weak directions required for the claim.
experiment_design.D_optimal_neighbor: Maximize log det I when local volume reduction is appropriate.
experiment_design.E_optimal_neighbor: Increase the smallest informative eigenvalue when one direction dominates uncertainty.
experiment_design.profile_guided: For nonlinear non-identifiability, simulate which new task, sampling time, perturbation or channel closes the open profile.

advance_if: Relevant gauge/label freedoms are resolved or quotient out.
Synthetic parameter/state recovery succeeds in the operating signal-to-noise regime.
Claim-supporting parameters or predictions have bounded uncertainty under reasonable variants.
advancement_gate.downgrade_if: Latent states or parameters remain underidentified while receiving strong substantive interpretation.

failure_conditions: Full Fisher rank is treated as proof of global/practical identifiability.
Local Gaussian uncertainty is reported despite strongly flat/asymmetric likelihood profiles.
An underidentified latent parameter receives strong psychological/spiritual interpretation because overall prediction is good.
More samples of the same uninformative channel are collected without checking information gain.
